configs.description: The chassis with two AC supplies and three fan modules fitted, front-to-rear air, before any part number: the shape every build below starts from.
configs.name: base

configs.description: Two DC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-1011-DC-RED supplies and FAN-7011H-F fan modules. The data sheet lists no DC part number for the switch; the supplies are spares, and a DC build is ordered through the "#" configurable SKUs.
configs.name: dc-f

configs.description: Two DC supplies and rear-to-front air: PWR-1011-DC-BLUE supplies and FAN-7011H-R fan modules. No DC part number is listed for the switch.
configs.name: dc-r

configs.description: The 7280CR3-32P4 with two AC supplies and front-to-rear air: PWR-1011-AC-RED supplies and FAN-7011H-F fan modules, all with red handles. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3-32P4-F.
configs.name: f

configs.description: The 7280CR3K-32P4A, the K build with an eight-core CPU, with front-to-rear air. The guide's Table 4 gives it 535 W typical and 851 W maximum, the same as the other builds (the data sheet says 543 W / 865 W). Ordered as DCS-7280CR3K-32P4A-F.
configs.name: k-a-f

configs.description: The 7280CR3K-32P4A with rear-to-front air. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3K-32P4A-R.
configs.name: k-a-r

configs.description: The 7280CR3K-32P4, the same hardware with 64 GB of memory and the large-routes licence, with front-to-rear air. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3K-32P4-F.
configs.name: k-f

configs.description: The 7280CR3K-32P4 with rear-to-front air. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3K-32P4-R.
configs.name: k-r

configs.description: The 7280CR3-32P4 with two AC supplies and rear-to-front air: PWR-1011-AC-BLUE supplies and FAN-7011H-R fan modules, all with blue handles. Ordered as DCS-7280CR3-32P4-R.
configs.name: r

gaps.note: The 7280CR3K-32P4A draws 535 W typical and 851 W maximum in the guide's Table 4 and 543 W / 865 W in the data sheet's comparison table (the figures the guide gives the 32D4A). The guide's Table 4 is used for the device.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: Storage temperature -25 to 70 C (guide Table 2) against -40 to 70 C (data sheet), and relative humidity 5 to 90 percent against 5 to 95 percent. The guide's, the older document by three months, are in attrs.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: The PWR-1011-DC input is "-40 to -60 VDC, 30 A" in guide Table 3 and "-48 to -60V DC" in the data sheet's power supply table. The guide's is in the component, the data sheet's in its provenance.
gaps.wanted: the maker's statement of which is current.

gaps.note: The 7280CR3K-32P4A has an eight-core CPU in place of a quad-core, and the K builds carry 64 GB of memory against 8 GB. No configuration can state a device attribute (the same open gap as cisco/asr-9001). The platform lines name all three.

The guide's Figures 3-1 to 3-4 are isometric drawings of another switch and carry no measure, and the kit guides for KIT-7001, KIT-7101-D and the other spares are not held, so no ear position or rail kit is written.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned drawing of the mounting bracket position, and the kit guides.

gaps.note: Figure C-3 draws four dots a QSFP port, but Table 10 describes one port LED and does not say what each of the four shows. All four are given Table 10's states.
gaps.wanted: the guide's account of the port lamps, or a photograph of the lit face.

gaps.note: The port-speed band's legends, the small print over each cage, the system and fan lamp glyphs and the PS1 and PS2 legends are unreadable in the 574 px figure. The glyphs and the two PS legends are drawn as read; the band and cage legends are not drawn.

Which side the latches of the stacked cages face is not visible in the figure. The library's convention is used for each cage type (QSFP upper cage upright, lower turned 180; OSFP both rows the same way up).
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the stacked cages.

gaps.note: The management block's arrow marks and its console symbol are drawn as the 7280CR3-32D4 draws them; the order of the three ports follows the datasheet's rear view and the library's other Arista stacks, and the figure's 1.24 px/mm resolves it only as three stacked ports.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of the rear management block.

gaps.note: The PWR-1011-DC supplies are drawn as the AC supply's housing with a plain two-pole terminal block. The guide shows a DC supply only in isometric figures; the real terminal arrangement is not drawn.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing or photograph of the PWR-1011-DC.

gaps.note: The guide's power tables and the data sheet give whole-switch figures only; the fan modules' missing power figure (lint L27) stands. The supplies state their output.
The 1RU grounding point is on the bottom of the chassis for KIT-GND-EXT-1RU (guide section 4.2, Table 5, Figure 4-2). No flat figure measures it, so it is not placed.
gaps.wanted: a flat drawing of the bottom with the grounding bracket holes.

chassis.note: Guide Table 1: 48.3 x 4.4 x 55.8 cm (19 x 1.75 x 22.0 in), 12.3 kg (27.0 lbs), the same for the 7280CR3-32P4, 7280CR3K-32P4 and 7280CR3K-32P4A. Data sheet: 43.99 x 4.37 x 55.83 cm (17.3 x 1.72 x 22.0 in), 27 lbs (12.27 kg). The width: 48.3 cm is over the mounting ears, so the body between them, which is what is modelled, is the data sheet's 43.99 cm (440.0 here), a 21.5 mm ear each side. The height is the data sheet's 43.7 (the guide rounds it to 4.4 cm). The depth is the data sheet's 558.3 (the guide's 55.8 cm is the same figure rounded). 1RU.

colour.note: The front plate is the 7280CR3-32D4's #aaabad, read there as the median of bare-plate pixels in the guide's figure of the same family.

configurations.note: Data sheet ordering information: DCS-7280CR3-32P4-F and -R, DCS-7280CR3K-32P4-F and -R, and DCS-7280CR3K-32P4A-F and -R ("front to rear air, 2 x AC" and "rear to front air, 2 x AC"). The "#" SKUs ("configurable fans and psu") and the "-M#" memory-expansion order are orders of parts, not part numbers a DCIM can hold, and are not listed. The data sheet lists no DC build of the switch: the PWR-1011-DC-RED and -BLUE supplies are spares, so the DC configurations are examples with no part number. The K and K-A builds share the base model's size, weight, figure and supplies and differ in memory, CPU and routes, which a configuration cannot state; each is a configuration with its own part numbers. There is no empty-bay (-S) configuration: no -S suffix exists in this family and the guide draws no blank for a power supply or fan module.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's Chapter 3 mounts the switch with the accessory-kit brackets and shows them in isometric drawings of a different switch ("Illustrations in this chapter depict the mounting of a DCS-7050QX-32S switch") that carry no measure. The data sheet lists the spares KIT-7001, KIT-2POST-1U-NT, KIT-4POST-NT, KIT-7001-4POST-L, KIT-7101-D, KIT-7101-RK, KIT-7101-LD-RK, KIT-ADJ-RLR and KIT-GND-EXT-1RU. No figure measures a bracket position, and the kit guides are not held, so no ear position is written and no rail kit is listed in chassis.kits. Recorded in the gap rack-ears.

environment.note: Guide Table 2: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -25 to 70 C, altitude 0 to 3,000 m, humidity 5 to 90 percent non-condensing. Data sheet: operating 0 to 40 C, storage -40 to 70 C, humidity 5 to 95 percent, altitude 0 to 3,000 m. Storage temperature and humidity differ: gap `environment`, the guide's used.

front-legend.note: The vertical legend up the left plate reads the maker's wordmark above the model "7280CR3-32P4" (read at 574 px; the print is small). THE WORDMARK IS NOT DRAWN: a logo-zone region is reserved over it and the plain model text is set. The figure's small print is not legible, so the text is as the guide's caption names the model.

front-ports.note: Figure C-3 at 1.273 px/mm, read in a ten-times enlargement. Thirty-two QSFP100 cages in two stacked rows (ports 1 to 32), in eight-column blocks of two groups of four columns: the column centres read 18.8, 37.8, 56.8 and 75.8 mm, then 107.9 to 164.9 for ports 9 to 16, then 261.3 to 318.3 for ports 17 to 24 and 350.8 to 407.8 for ports 25 to 32. The column pitch inside a group is 19.0 (the registry's ganged-QSFP pitch) and the gap between groups is 13.3 mm wider than a column. The row centres read from the white number tabs at 14.7 and 30.4 mm down, a row pitch of 15.7. Four OSFP cages (33 over 34 at 200.5 mm, 35 over 36 at 227.0 mm) sit between the blocks in yellow boxes 4.3 to 20.8 and 24.4 to 40.5 mm down, so their centres are 12.55 and 32.45 mm down. std/osfp@1 (23.1 x 13.5) is seated. The belly-to-belly orientation of the QSFP cages is the library's convention (upper cage upright, lower turned 180); the OSFP cages sit the same way up, which is the library's convention for stacked OSFP cages (lint L108). The figure is too small to show the latch side.

fru-bays.note: Guide Appendix E (E.2 power supplies, E.3 fan modules) gives removal and installation procedures, and the data sheet calls the supplies "1+1 hot-swappable" and the fans "hot-swap". SO THE TWO POWER SUPPLIES AND THE THREE FAN MODULES ARE BAYS. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit. The management block, the USB port and the console port are part of the chassis and are placements.

gate-1-front.note: Figure C-3 passes. The raster is 574 x 116 pixels; the body measures 561 px wide and 56 px tall (aspect 10.0), against the data sheet's 440.0 / 43.7 = 10.07, so the figure is near-orthographic and carries geometry at 1.273 px/mm (the 440 mm body is the scale anchor, its left edge read at 8.7 px as for the sibling 7280CR3-32D4 face). One pixel is 0.8 mm, so every position is good to about 0.8 mm, and every one is `estimated` because it is read off a picture and no dimension states it. The old guide's Figure 49 is the same 574 x 116 raster, compared pixel for pixel (no pixel differs), so it is a repeat of the source and not a second reading. The status lamps are read from the green pixels of the lamps (550 px), which put them about 5 mm left of where the sibling 7280CR3-32D4 file puts its lamps.

gate-1-rear.note: Figure D-2 is a 552 x 126 px raster whose chassis is 544 px between its edges and 52 px tall (aspect 10.5; the 3 percent excess is the cut-off bottom edge), 1.239 px/mm over the 440 mm body; positions are good to about 0.8 mm. The guide draws the rear generically (D-1 to D-4) and does not say which model uses which. The 7280CR3-32P4 is mapped to D-2 by its three fan modules (data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 3 (N+1 redundant)"), its 1RU height, its two power supplies and its management ports at the rear (Figure C-3 has none at the front). THE MAPPING IS ESTIMATED. The positions are the 7280CR3-32D4's, which is mapped to the same figure.

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. EOS names ports Ethernet1 to Ethernet36 and Management1; this is the vendor's convention and no held document prints it.

lifecycle.note: Searched 2026-10-23 (web searches of Arista's end-of-sale notices) for a notice for the 7280CR3-32P4, 7280CR3K-32P4 and 7280CR3K-32P4A: none found. The notices the searches returned were for older 7280 models (which name the 32P4 as a replacement) and for the 7280SR3K-48YC8 (notice 23789) and 7280CR3K-36S (notice 23790) series, not for this one.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat. The guide's installation figures are isometric. Each carries an `empty` sentence. The 1RU grounding point is on the bottom of the chassis (guide section 4.2, Table 5, KIT-GND-EXT-1RU, Figure 4-1 shows the 7280CR3-32P4); no figure measures it.

port-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.2, Table 10: "Port LEDs near their corresponding ports provide a link and operational status": off the link is down, green link up, yellow software disabled, flashing yellow failed diagnostics. Figure C-3 draws a row of four dark dots above each upper QSFP column and four below each lower one (the guide's Figure A-3 captions four dots "Port 4 LEDs"). FOUR LAMPS A QSFP PORT are modelled, a to d, 4.0 mm apart and centred on the column (the dots read 3.9 mm apart at 7.5 mm down above the upper cage and 37.3 mm down below the lower one). Table 10 gives one set of states, so all four carry it; what each of the four means is the gap port-lamp-count. The OSFP cages carry no lamp the figure shows (white light-pipe bars only).

port-numbering.note: Figure C-3 (callout 5, "Port numbers") prints 1 over 2, 3 over 4, and so on down each column and across, 1 to 32 in the two blocks, then 33 over 34 and 35 over 36 in the OSFP columns, which sit between ports 16 and 17 in space but are numbered after 32. The odd number is the upper cage. The figure prints each number on a white tab over the cage opening; a seated cage hides what is painted under it, so the numerals are set in the band between the two rows, the odd number left of its column centre and the even one right of it. EOS interface names are not printed on the metal and are not modelled.

power.note: Guide Table 4: typical / maximum 535 W / 851 W for the 7280CR3-32P4, the 7280CR3K-32P4 and the 7280CR3K-32P4A (unlike the 32D4A, the 32P4A draws the same), each with PWR-1011-AC or PWR-1011-DC. The data sheet's comparison table gives the K-32P4A 543 W / 865 W (gap `size-conflict`); the guide's Table 4 is used, and the data sheet's typical is "measured at 25C ambient with 50% load on all ports".

rear.note: Figure D-2 at 1.239 px/mm, the rear seen from behind with x = 0 at the left of the drawing. PS1 is the left and PS2 the right (callouts 1 and 10). Each power supply module is 73.5 mm wide (the data sheet's "73.5MM") at 4.0 and 362.3 mm across and 1.85 mm down. The management block is a grey plate 83.0 to 101.0 mm across with the Ethernet management port, the USB port and the RJ-45 console port stacked in it, in the order the library draws other Arista management stacks. Three fan modules 78.6 mm wide at 107.7, 191.0 and 274.3 mm across (an 83.3 mm pitch) and 2.55 mm down.

rear-fan.note: Data sheet: "Hot-swappable Fans 3 (N+1 redundant)", "Fan Tray FAN-7011H", FAN-7011H-F (front-to-rear) and FAN-7011H-R (rear-to-front) as spares. Guide section 2.1: a red handle is an air-exit module and a blue handle an air-inlet one, and every module must have the same direction. The three fan modules are bays that accept FAN-7011H-F or -R; the -R configurations seat the blue modules.

sources.note: 7280R3 Series Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, document DOC-07041-01, 63 pages, PDF created 2025-05-16 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280R3.pdf): Table 1 (dimensions and weights), Table 2 (operating and storage), Table 3 (power input), Table 4 (power draw and supported supplies), section 2.1 (airflow orientation, handle colour), Table 5 (grounding), section 4.5 (serial and management cables), Appendix A (status indicators, Tables 9 to 13), Appendix C (Figure C-3, the front panel of the DCS-7280CR3-32P4, 7280CR3K-32P4 and 7280CR3K-32P4A), Appendix D (Figure D-2, the rear panel with three fan modules), Appendix E (field replacement). 7280 Data Center Switches Quick Start Guide, Arista Networks, 58 pages, PDF created 2022-06-03 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/qsg/qsg-books/QS_7280_1RU_Gen3.pdf): Figure 49 (DCS-7280CR3-32P4 and 7280CR3K-32P4), the cross-check of Figure C-3. 7280R3 Series Data Center Switch Router Data Sheet, Arista Networks, 03-0045-59, dated August 11th, 2025 (https://www.arista.com/assets/data/pdf/Datasheets/7280R3-Data-Sheet.pdf): the model comparison of the 7280CR3-32P4, CR3K-32P4 and CR3K-32P4A, the power supply specifications and the ordering information. Held and checked first: intake COVERAGE.md and SOURCES.md, which list no photograph, Visio stencil, 3D model or CAD file for this model (Arista publishes none; the stencil zip could not be fetched). The data sheet's picture of the face is a thumbnail. No drawing, photograph or logo is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings.

speed-strips.note: Guide Figure C-3 callout 6, "Port-speed group": a thin grey band between the two rows carries small legends at each pair of columns (read as "A8" and "M*" style marks) and the OSFP columns sit on a grey plate with two screws at each end. The legends are unreadable at 85 ppi and are not drawn; the plate and the four screws are drawn.

status-lamps.note: Guide Appendix A.1.1, Table 9 and Figure C-3 callouts 1 to 4: a system status lamp (blinking green on power-up, green normal, blue locator, amber for two or more failed fans), a fan status lamp (green, amber for one module removed or failed, red for two or more) and a status lamp for each of the two power supplies (green operating, off removed or faulty). Four lamps in a column at 425.6 mm, 3.2 mm apart from 5.2 mm down. The printed glyphs beside them are a system symbol, a fan symbol and two small legends read as PS1 and PS2.

vents.note: The figure shows a perforated strip along the top (0.4 to 5.5 mm down), grids of dark squares in the gaps between the port groups (86.9 to 96.9, 177.4 to 186.9, 240.5 to 250.0 and 329.5 to 339.5 mm across, 7.5 to 39.5 down), a grid left of port 1, and a ribbed strip of vertical slits along the bottom lip (39.3 to 43.2 mm down). Each is drawn as a vent field in its measured extent; the individual squares are not drawn one by one.
